subphase: S66: diagnose the candidate-only xilinx-bootgen signing segfault (STOP-class candidate)

execution.note: all builds, probes and workload runs executed inside the expansion court container; the host ran no project command. The host working tree was clean before the receipt and is clean except for this receipt after it.

verdict.summary: RSA_get0_d returns a valid, live BIGNUM whose value is identical to the authority's (BN_num_bits(d)=4093, BN_bn2hex identical). bootgen then reads the private BIGNUM field ->d from its own copy of OpenSSL 1.0's struct bignum_st. BIGNUM is opaque in both the authority's and the candidate's public headers (types.h:96), so that read is undefined behaviour. It happens to work against the authority because OpenSSL's private bignum_st starts with BN_ULONG *d; under the candidate the first word of our opaque representation is the Vec capacity (65 = 0x41), so the consumer copies from address 0x41 and faults. No src/ fix is appropriate (AGENTS.md section 17: do not reproduce UB; never imitate a flawed implementation and call it correctness).
verdict.ledger_effect: No change to the campaign's memory-safety defect ledger: this is not a candidate memory-safety defect. xilinx-bootgen does not graduate; its measured grade stays L5-loaded and its cause is now adjudicated.

candidate.built_from: a4e511865 (src/ is byte-identical from that commit to HEAD 3ea2887fc; git diff a4e511865..HEAD -- src/ is empty)

commands.backtrace_method: no gdb in the court image; a SIGSEGV/SIGBUS/SIGABRT handler in a preloaded .so (LD_PRELOAD) prints si_addr, RIP and backtrace(); the faulting PC is resolved with addr2line against the unstripped consumer and disassembled against libc

reproducer_sha256.freeprobe.c: (mimic of the consumer's private-layout write followed by BN_free; see negative_control)

authority_verify.observed: Authentication is verified on bootimage signed.bin

fault.fault_is_in: consumer (xilinx-bootgen); the faulting memcpy is bootgen's, reading a consumer-computed pointer. No frame is inside libcrypto.
backtrace: bootgen(+0x1d414)  Key::ParseOpenSSLKey(_IO_FILE*)   <-- return address of the memcpy call

same_pattern_elsewhere: authkeys.cpp:231-232  memcpy(N, RSA_get0_n(rsa)->d, keySize); memcpy(E, RSA_get0_e(rsa)->d, sizeof(uint32_t));

consumer_private_definition.struct: struct bignum_st { BN_ULONG *d; int top; int dmax; int neg; int flags; };
consumer_private_definition.note: copied from OpenSSL 1.0; xil-bignum.h is included beside the real (opaque) openssl/bn.h so the private field access compiles

public_contract.conclusion: BIGNUM is opaque in both; neither library promises a layout. The consumer's complete definition makes its access an incompatible-type access across translation units (undefined behaviour), tolerated by the authority only because its private struct begins with BN_ULONG *d.

why_the_value_is_zero_and_the_accessor_i.measured_authority_bignum_d_words: d(limb ptr)=0x55..df60, top=0x40, dmax=0x40, neg=0, flags=5
why_the_value_is_zero_and_the_accessor_i.vec_layout_in_this_build: the candidate's BigNum has #[repr(C)] { d: Vec<Limb>, neg: c_int, flags: c_int }; rustc 1.98.1 lays Vec out as (cap, ptr, len), so the first word is the capacity. A probe (Vec::with_capacity(10) + 3 pushes) measured words = [0xa, <ptr>, 0x3].
why_the_value_is_zero_and_the_accessor_i.accessor_validity_proof: BN_num_bits(RSA_get0_d(rsa)) = 4093, BN_num_bits(RSA_get0_n(rsa)) = 4096, and BN_bn2hex of both is byte-identical to the authority's; the BIGNUM pointer itself is non-null and live. The accessor returns the right object; only the consumer's interpretation of its opaque contents is wrong.
disassembly_of_the_decisive_site: bootgen+0x1d409  mov (%rax),%rsi           ; consumer reads private field ->d
bootgen+0x1d414  <return address seen on the faulting stack>

trigger.verify_path_manifestation: The verification path (verifyimage-zynqmp.cpp:95-110) instead *writes* the 1.0 layout into a live BN_new() object (batches d/top/dmax/neg/flags). The candidate's Vec ends up with len=0 (the consumer's flags/neg land on our len word), so RSA_public_encrypt sees a zero modulus and returns an error; exit 1, no crash. The authority's BIGNUM happens to accept those writes, so verification proceeds. Same consumer UB, different symptom.

negative_control.purpose: Show the consumer pattern is unsafe under the authority too, so the divergence is not a candidate-only memory-safety defect.
negative_control.probe: BN_new(); write struct xil_bignum_st fields (d=buf, top=64, dmax=64, neg=0, flags=0); BN_free(b).
negative_control.candidate: SIGSEGV (exit 139): the corrupted Vec is deallocated from consumer-supplied cap/ptr.
negative_control.authority: SIGABRT (exit 134): glibc 'munmap_chunk(): invalid pointer' while freeing the consumer-supplied d.
negative_control.interpretation: bootgen survives only because it does not free the private-layout RSA/BIGNUM it constructed in the verify path (leak) and because the authority's private layout happens to line up in the sign path. The authority's tolerance is accidental, not a contract.

divergence.agents_md_section: 17 (divergence classification; UB in the C authority / consumer not reproduced)
divergence.class: consumer undefined behaviour (private BIGNUM layout) tolerated by the authority's incidental representation
divergence.consequence: xilinx-bootgen cannot sign (SIGSEGV) or verify (error exit 1) against the candidate; it remains at L5-loaded. The same consumer source is unsafe against OpenSSL 1.1+ as a matter of contract and would misbehave under any opaque BIGNUM whose first word is not the limb pointer.
divergence.treatment: Do not reproduce the private layout. The correct repair is consumer-side: use BN_bn2binpad(RSA_get0_d(...), D, keySize) / BN_bn2binpad(RSA_get0_n(...), N, keySize) and the public exponent accessors, rather than ->d. The court keeps the pristine upstream source; no consumer patch was applied and no pass was manufactured.
divergence.compatibility_scope: a functional workload over a pristine consumer that relies on undefined behaviour; the authority completed it only by layout accident
divergence.not_an_src_contract_breach: RSA_get0_d/RSA_get0_n/RSA_get0_e return the correct BIGNUM pointers; no ownership state, out-parameter write, or success code is wrong.

src_change.regression_test_rationale: No src/ defect was found, so no src/ regression test is owed. The standing evidence is the probe above, which fails against both subjects, and the re-measurement below.

output: [p1000  435] xilinx-bootgen candidate L5-loaded        the consumer did not sign the fixture
remeasurement.atlas_disposition: the measurement wrote forensics/downstream/runtime-functional-atlas.json; the committed bytes were restored (sha256 7e8554dfc8c43ac2c265ea7bd17baa463bb94fc7b183cde6b50aaa83c5142ab4) so this subphase's diff is limited to this receipt. The re-measurement confirms the S65 grades exactly.

non_claims: This is not a candidate memory-safety defect and does not confirm a use-after-free or an out-of-bounds write in src/.
The invalid read is inside the consumer; no libcrypto frame appears in the faulting chain.

A functional pass for xilinx-bootgen is not claimed, and the grade is not raised; the authority's pass is recorded as accidental-layout tolerance, not as a standard the candidate must reproduce by imitating UB.
No claim is made about other consumers that may poke BIGNUM internals; each would need its own measurement.
The negative control demonstrates the authority also aborts if the same private-layout object is freed; it does not certify anything about the authority's general robustness.
followups: Keep xilinx-bootgen at L5-loaded with this adjudicated cause; do not add a consumer patch to manufacture L7.

If an opaque-BIGNUM-layout canary is wanted for future courts, use the negative-control probe above as a test-only detector of consumers that read private BIGNUM fields; keep it out of release artefacts.
